connector.why: Same reading: a tzaddik's years are complete because even the childhood years before he knew his Creator count, via 'lecha tal yaldutecha' (BR 39:8); RT cross-refers it.

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:39
connector.why: Develops Isaac's 'va'ochal mikol' (BR 67) as a taste of the World-to-Come meal, as here; context is Adar/Nisan and Purim, not Abraham's life.
Shares only Vayikra Rabbah 21; it expounds 'ori' = Rosh Hashanah, while the maamar uses 'yishi' = Yom Kippur.
Tal yaldutecha: Abraham's idolatrous early years 'evaporate' and he becomes 'Eitan HaEzrachi'; same midrash, different focus (Abraham called Israel).
Isaac's 'mikol' from Bava Batra 17a and BR 67 = taste of the World to Come, without the evil inclination; same derashah, applied to wine.
Explains bakol/mikol/kol for the three Patriarchs, with Jacob combining his fathers' attributes; same structure, different explanation (sight vs. substance of the good).
Tal yaldutecha: Abraham's beginning in idolatry is part of his praise, plus the ten trials ending in the Akeidah; touches the maamar's childhood-years and last-trial themes.

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8:4
connector.why: Mentions in passing that Abraham reached 'Eitan HaEzrachi'/tal yaldutecha through effort; main subject is three kinds of wisdom (Adam, Noah, Abraham).

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 15:2
connector.why: Abraham's own effort (hishtadlut), 'lech lecha' and tal yaldutecha; but it argues the effort itself is from God, a different direction from the maamar.
Tal yaldutecha: Abraham was holy 'from the womb' and could transform his past once Isaac was born; shares the childhood-years idea.
Abraham as 'head of those who exert themselves', 'hit'halech' = effort; touches the maamar's moving-not-standing theme, but its subject is Torah against imagination and Purim.
Jacob takes Torah ('emet le-Yaakov', Berakhot 5b) and comprises his fathers' attributes, with the Yerushalmi on giving God the heart; parallels the maamar's Jacob section.

connector.ref: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 25:4
connector.why: Bakol/mikol/kol: Jacob had 'kol' constantly, his bed complete; same derashah and the same claim that Jacob is the complete one.
'Yafah sichatan shel avdei avot' (BR 60): a great man's casual talk is Torah; Eliezer's merit is Abraham's merit. Supports the maamar's point on this parashah's secrets.
Shares only Bereshit Rabbah 60, a different passage there (R. Pinchas ben Yair's donkey); subject is three levels of love of God.

candidates.why: Quotes and develops the same Zohar (Chayei Sarah 131b) the maamar expounds: Torah is all life in both worlds, frees from the Angel of Death, and 'the evil serpent that darkened the world cannot rule' over one who toils in it.

Eliezer relies on Abraham's merit to bring about the miraculous match, as in the Zohar the maamar cites ('zechuteih de-Avraham'); but it denies the test was about Rebecca's kindness, which the maamar stresses.

Commentary on the very Zohar passage ('de-oraita kol chayin... chayin de-inun chayin'): long days in the World to Come come from Arich Anpin; Rav Tzadok likewise traces this life to Atika. It also takes up the question about Moses.
Reads 'zaken ba bayamim... berach bakol' as the plain story of Eliezer's oath and mission; no development of 'asher chai', bakol/mikol/kol or the Zohar.

candidates.ref: Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Derush al HaTorah 18:13-14
candidates.why: Brings Bava Batra 16b-17a with Maharal (Derekh Chayyim 6): the Patriarchs' taste of the World to Come was from their own share there, with no break. This is the same derashah the maamar uses.
Quotes the same Yerushalmi 'liba ve-eina... hen yahavt li libach ve-einach' (at 7:23) and makes the heart the root; the maamar uses it on 'ha'er eineinu... ve-dabek libenu'.

candidates.ref: Sidduro Shel Shabbat, Volume II, Derush I 1:5-6
candidates.why: Expounds the Bnei Heichala song at the third meal ('le-mechezei ziv Ze'ir Anpin', 'ra'ava de-ra'avin') as the hour of 'nachalat Yaakov'; the maamar likewise makes the third meal Jacob's time of favor.

found.why: Reads 'lech lecha' with the same Zohar 'le-atkana darga dilach' as moving from 'amidah' (acceptance of the yoke) to 'halichah', cleaving in love. This is Rav Tzadok's moving rather than standing, as Abraham's attribute of love.
The Piaseczner: one who has not grown this year has not really lived it; 'Avraham zaken ba bayamim': the Abraham of today, not of yesterday. Same reading of a life counted only by continual growth.

found.ref: Zera Kodesh, On Torah, Chayei Sara 4
found.why: The doubled 'chayei Avraham asher chai' means life drawn from supernal Chochmah through Torah ('ha-chochmah techayeh'); parallels the maamar's 'asher chai' as life from its source through Torah, though it says Chochmah where Rav Tzadok says Atika.

On Bava Batra 16b-17a: the Patriarchs tasted their own share of the World to Come in this world, with no break as the World to Come has none. This is the bakol/mikol/kol derashah the maamar applies to the three Patriarchs.

footnotes.text:
**Nefesh HaChayim, Gate IV 17** (Machshava) — R. Chaim of Volozhin gathers the sources that Torah protects in both worlds and closes with this same Zohar (Chayei Sarah 131b): Torah study frees from the Angel of Death, and had Adam held to the Tree of Life, which is Torah, he would not have brought death. Like Rav Tzadok, he reads the serpent's loss of power as freedom from death.
וע״ד כל מאן דאשתדל באורייתא לא יכיל לשלטאה עלוי ההוא חויא בישא דאחשיך עלמא

**Ohr HaChammah on Zohar I 131b (1:262)** (Kabbalah) — R. Avraham Azulai on this very passage: 'complete life' has no lack, 'life that is truly life' is the true life rather than bodily life, and 'long days' in the World to Come flow from Arich Anpin. Rav Tzadok likewise traces 'all these kinds of life' to their source in Atika.
וליומין אריכין מצד ארך אנפין לעלמא דאתי

**Be'er Mayim Chaim, Genesis 24:42** (Chassidus) — Eliezer knew he was not worthy to have his sign answered; the God of Abraham made it happen 'for Abraham's sake', since Abraham had made His divinity known. This parallels the Zohar's 'Abraham's merit went out to meet that servant' as Rav Tzadok reads it.
וזכותו הוא שיעמוד כאן להראות לי האשה אשר הוכיח לבן אדוני

**Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:23** (Kabbalah) — R. Eliyahu de Vidas quotes the same derashah of 'the heart and the eye, the two brokers of sin' and shows that the heart is the source of every trait, which is why the verse puts the heart before the eyes. Rav Tzadok reads the blessing's 'enlighten our eyes… make our heart cleave' as giving God both.
הן יהבת לי לבך ועינך אנא ידענא דאת לי

footnotes.ref: Sidduro Shel Shabbat, Volume II, Derush I 1:5-6
footnotes.text:
**Sidduro Shel Shabbat II, Derush 1:5–6** (Chassidus) — R. Chaim of Czernowitz explains the third-meal song Bnei Heichala ('yearning to behold the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin', 'ra'ava de-ra'avin') as the hour when the light of Jacob's boundless inheritance shines on Israel. This parallels Rav Tzadok's third meal as Jacob's time of favor.
הוא בחי נחלת יעקב אביכם נחלה בלא מצרים

**Shem MiShmuel, Lech Lecha 7:7** (Chassidus) — Until 'lech lecha' Abraham stood firm through acceptance of the yoke of Heaven (amidah). He was now commanded to move on to halichah, cleaving in love, which the Zohar calls 'le-atkana darga dilach'. Like Rav Tzadok, he makes Abraham's love the attribute of a life that keeps moving rather than standing still.
אלא יאחז צדיק דרכו בחי' הליכה היינו להתדבק באהבה אל הארץ אשר אראך

**Tzav VeZeruz 2** (Chassidus) — The Piaseczner Rebbe: set yourself a picture each year of who you must become; if you have not grown toward it, you have not truly gained another year, for only the person of last year 'lived'. 'Abraham was old, come into days' means the Abraham of today, not of yesterday. This is Rav Tzadok's 'all his years he was alive, continually growing'.
ואברהם זקן בא בימים, אברהם של היום, הי׳ של היום, ולא האברהם של אתמול.

footnotes.ref: Zera Kodesh, On Torah, Chayei Sara 4
footnotes.text:
**Zera Kodesh, Chayei Sara 4** (Chassidus) — R. Naftali of Ropshitz: the doubled wording 'chayei Avraham asher chai' points to life drawn from supernal Chochmah through Torah ('wisdom gives life to those who have it'), which Abraham reached by keeping the whole Torah. This parallels Rav Tzadok's reading of 'asher chai' as life from its supernal source, reached through the Torah that 'is all life'.
ולכן כתיב ואלה שני חיי אברהם אשר חי הוכפל הלשון להורות על המשכה מחכמה עליונה
